inputs.seed_note: no random numbers are drawn in P7

choices.why: Spec P7: the spanwise airload by Schrenk's approximation checked against the study's vortex lattice, inertia relief, shear and bending by Raymer's station method, caps in bending and the web in shear and shear buckling, high-strength graphite/epoxy with a banded knock-down factor, at limit load times 1.5 in the ruled cases, with the P5 row 4 cases as a sensitivity.

library.schrenk: (14.9)-(14.11), p. 343: trapezoidal chord, area, elliptical chord of the same span and area; the load shape is the average of the two, scaled to the required lift and carried to the centreline (p. 342-343)
library.trim_first: p. 342: a trim calculation gives the tail lift, which raises or lowers the wing lift the load factor needs
library.station_method: p. 381-383, Figs. 14.37-14.39: about ten to twenty stations, distributed loads as concentrated loads by the trapezoid rule of Fig. 14.39 (F = S(a + b)/2 at X = S(2a + b)/(3a + 3b) from the end of intensity b), shear summed from the tip inward, moment as the area under the shear curve
library.wing_weight_by_chord: p. 382: wing weight can be spread in proportion to chord; weights are multiplied by the load factor (Fig. 14.38)
library.spar_idealisation: p. 384-385, Fig. 14.41: the caps take all the bending, the web, taken as the full spar depth, all the shear at a uniform stress
library.material_table: Table 14.4, p. 368-369: typical composite properties at room temperature; p. 368 calls them typical values only
library.page_check: The pages themselves could not be opened in this session: `uv run alex page raymer-aircraft-design-conceptual 368` stops with "sources/raymer-aircraft-design-conceptual.pdf is missing", and the Drive connector refused the book's download (file over its 10 MB limit). The values below are read from the library's chapter notes (unit 13, `verified: true`), whose QA file (library/raymer-aircraft-design-conceptual/qa.md) records Table 14.4's nine rows over both pages as checked against the page image ("Correct"; only the title misprint "properues" is flagged). They were read twice on 2026-11-28 (the notes' table as text, and the same rows parsed cell by cell); both reads agree. Not from memory. A check against the printed page stays open for the Fable review (PD-22).

material.name: High-strength graphite/epoxy, fibre volume 60 %, Table 14.4, p. 368-369
material.units: density lb/in^3; strengths and moduli psi (the table prints 10^3 psi and 10^6 psi)

knock_down.applies_to: the strengths F_tu, F_cu (caps) and F_su (web); not the moduli
knock_down.source: Judgement [Not lib]: no open source was opened for it. Raymer p. 368 calls Table 14.4 typical values; design values must also cover environment (hot and wet), impact damage, scatter (a statistical basis) and the holes and joints of a built spar. One factor of one half on the typical strengths, with the band run at both ends as a sensitivity.

geometry.spar_chord_fraction: the P3 arrangement's front_spar_chord_fraction (data/task12/pd_p3_arrangement.yaml): one bending spar there
geometry.section: NACA 4415, the loft's section (P2, P3); depth measured straight up between the surfaces at the spar's chord station, geometry3d/sections.py

skin_thickness_in.source: Judgement [Not lib]: upper and lower skin over the caps; the cap fits inside the section depth less two skins

cap_width_over_chord.source: Judgement [Not lib]: flange width of each cap as a share of the local chord, centred on the spar station

web_buckling_K.source: Fig. 14.42, p. 386, simply supported edges, long panel: 'toward about 5.5, read from the graph' in the library's notes (unit 14). Simply supported is the lower of the two curves; the web panel is taken as long (rib spacing at least the spar depth)

geometry.web_panel_width: the spar depth inside the skins (Raymer p. 384-385 takes the web as the full spar depth)

loads.factor_of_safety: r0's Nz_ultimate over its limit load factor (5.7 / 3.8 = 1.5; PD-9)

stations.source: Raymer p. 382-383: about ten to twenty stations; extra stations where a load starts, ends or acts as a point

loads.airload: Schrenk's shape over the full span, scaled to the wing lift of the case after the tail's trim load; the larger of Schrenk's and the lattice's root bending moment is used (spec P7 row 2)

lattice.code: drone/vlm.py (the study's own vortex lattice, Task 10 rows V6a-V6c)
lattice.planform: r0's wing, trapezoidal, unswept leading edge, untwisted (drone/geometry.tapered)

inertia_relief.wing: r0's wing weight, spread over the span in proportion to chord (Raymer p. 382)
inertia_relief.fuel: in the P4 tanks on the P3 loft (runs/task12/pd/2026-11-27/p4/p4.json, tanks): between their span stations in proportion to chord squared (the tank's section area); full at take-off weight, none at zero-fuel weight
inertia_relief.points: sponsons and main gear (r0 component weights), half to each side, at r0's main-wheel half track
inertia_relief.left_out: fuel system, flight controls and every other item (no relief taken for them; the wing loads are higher for it)

loads.trim: P4's tail_cl_trim (prelim/p4_methods.py; Raymer (16.7), p. 416, without thrust terms) with P4's as-arranged layout and P2's section moment (both from runs/task12/pd/2026-11-27/p4/p4.json), at the centre of gravity of the case's weight (P4 row 1: payload on, gear up, nominal empty weight; full fuel at take-off weight, empty at zero-fuel weight). The wing and tail lift together equal n W. Every case is taken balanced in pitch, gusts included.

cases_sensitivity.name: CS-23 gust speeds, up and down (P5 row 4)
cases_sensitivity.from: P5 row4 cases cs23_speeds: the point of largest n_up and of lowest n_down

cases_sensitivity.name: gust held at 30 ft/s above V_C, up and down (P5 row 4)
cases_sensitivity.from: P5 row4 cases ruled_held_30: the point of largest n_up and of lowest n_down

loads.speed_of_a_case: each manoeuvre case is evaluated at every speed listed; the speed with the largest ultimate root bending moment in magnitude is the case's speed

sizing.rule: every station sized to the envelope of the ruled cases at ultimate load: caps from (14.35) with the caps alone in bending; web the larger of the shear-strength and the shear-buckling thickness
sizing.margins: margin of safety = allowable over stress less 1, per station and case; the governing ruled case is at 0 by construction
sizing.fit: the caps fit if the cap area equation has a real root: the two caps and two skins inside the section depth
sizing.not_sized: rear spar (closes the tank, carries torsion: PD-9 has no torsion box), ribs, skins, joints, fasteners; no minimum gauge

r1.layout: P4b's chosen layout (PD-21) and its centre of gravity at full and empty fuel (runs/task12/pd/2026-11-28/p4b/p4b.json), every weight raised by its empty-weight change
r1.CL_max: P2's measured clean wing maximum lift (runs/task12/pd/2026-11-27/p2b/p2.json, wing.measured.clean) for the positive corner speed

row2.evidence_class: partly independent (the study's own vortex lattice against Schrenk's approximation, same planform)

cases.name: gust held at 30 ft/s above V_C, up (P5 row 4)
gust held at 30 ft/s above V_C, down (P5 row 4)

row1.note: the elliptic check on the run's own stations is reported, not judged: the tolerance is for the method, on the check grid

row3.evidence_class: coding check of the sizing (every station is sized to the envelope of the ruled cases, so the governing case is at zero margin by construction); the content is whether a sizing exists and what margin the other cases keep

row4.evidence_class: layout construction on the loft's section with an assumed skin

row5.evidence_class: independent of the statistical wing weight (bottom-up spar, typical material values with a judged knock-down); no tolerance
